Years ago, MacBooks came with a slot that allowed you to secure your device to a table leg or similar object with a cable lock. It was especially useful in coffee shops, so you didn't have to lug your computer around when you went back to the counter for another drink.

Those slots disappeared long ago, but you can now buy an adapter to add a security lock to your MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, or MacBook Pro...

If you've been a long-time MacBook user, you might remember the security slots built into both sides of the chassis. These slots were designed for T-shaped accessories — insert the accessory into the slot and turn it 90 degrees to lock it. The most common design was a cable loop that could be threaded through a table leg in a coffee shop or library.

CompuLock is now bringing back that concept, offering adapters that mount to the corner or edge of a MacBook so you can attach a cable lock. The adapter uses a two-piece design, clamping onto the MacBook with screws.

The company has now added a MacBook Neo version alongside the existing MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models.

It's important to point out that these locks have always been extremely low-security devices, designed only to stop someone from grabbing your MacBook and running off in the space of a few seconds. I've used one of these locks in a small coffee shop where I could still see my table while going to the counter to top up my tea; but if I wanted my MacBook completely out of sight, I wouldn't rely on this kind of lock.

At $70, the adapter isn't cheap, especially since you'd still need to buy a lock separately; but if you happen to have a spare lock lying around in a drawer, you might want to give it a new lease of life.
